tip: Mid-sentence adverbs like ofta go between har and the participle: Vi har ofta undrat, not har undrat ofta.
Swedish uses the 24-hour clock for schedules, so avgår klockan 14:35 means departs at 2:35 pm.
A whole clause can fill the first slot. Vad han sa works as the subject, so the verb förvånade comes right after it.
Front the object for emphasis and the verb stays in second place, so the subject jag follows: Henne har jag aldrig träffat.
Front an infinitive for emphasis and the verb still comes second: Springa puts orkar before the subject jag.
The -s ending forms a passive: syns means is seen or is visible, so Jag syns inte = I cannot be seen.
Starting with a restrictive adverb like sällan forces inversion, so the verb har comes before the subject jag.
The -s ending can mean each other: kramas is hug one another, so Vi kramas = we hug each other.
